correctness.rationale: Proof controls path lengths through the diameter, shows any two covering paths overlap in at most one vertex, eliminates a path spanning both hubs unless the two shortest arms have length two, and forces exclusive/shared-arm geodesic inequalities. These give the sole parity exceptions. Every case has explicit shortest-path witnesses; three geodesics always suffice. The integer-only verifier checks all 455 triples up to 14, 80 wider triples, and 1,140 explicit constructions through 19. The infinite claim rests on proof rather than computation.

evidence: Chakraborty–Defrain–Foucaud–Mari–Tale, arXiv:2610.22010v1, Theorems 1.1–1.3, concern complexity at bounded pathwidth and an algorithm parameterized by treewidth and diameter, rather than an exact value for each theta graph.
Chakraborty–Foucaud–Hakanen FCT 2023, Section 5, presents an edge-geodesic covering bound as a function of cyclomatic number, not a full vertex-IP classification of theta graphs.
Chakraborty et al., ISAAC 2022, analyze chordal, interval, chordality- and treelength-based approximations, with no claimed exact three-arm theta result.

Chakraborty–Foucaud–Hakanen, full expanded arXiv:2509.00383v1, Theorems 21 and 22: for theta graphs with cyclomatic number two and zero leaves, the proved edge cover bound is at most seven and the vertex isometric-path partition bound is at most four. These are not exact minimum covering values.

Dumas–Foucaud–Perez–Todinca (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2024), Theorem 2, bounds pathwidth given an existing cover of prescribed size; Theorem 3 gives an algorithm with terminals. Neither direction characterizes when a given theta graph has a two-path cover.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general algorithm for computing the quantity, or an upper bound specialized to cyclomatic number two, does not imply which of the infinitely many three-arm graphs admit a two-path cover or the two exceptional parity conditions; the inspected primary statements do not provide stronger coverage.

evidence: The vertex-isometric-path number (also called isometric path cover number or vertex geodesic cover number) is defined as a minimum number of shortest paths covering vertices in Fisher–Fitzpatrick (2001) and Manuel (2021).

Manuel–Klavžar (2018), Proposition 2.1, gives the general-position number for equal-arm theta graphs, and Section 3 gives inequalities relating that invariant to isometric covers; neither gives the present vertex-cover minimum.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The names are equivalent definitions of the same optimization problem, so title differences were not treated as novelty. The equal-arm theta general-position result is a maximum set subject to no triple on a geodesic; an upper bound involving ip cannot be inverted into the exact parity classification.
